text:
kate: Quick heads-up: running into duplicated partial tokens after short reconnects using SSE resume. Client reconnects with Last-Event-ID and then the resumed stream repeats the last partial chunk, producing doubled text fragments. :grimacing:

kate: Super minimal repro I used (browser + curl):
1) open streaming endpoint (EventSource or curl -H 'Accept: text/event-stream')
2) cause a brief network hiccup (~150-300ms)
3) client reconnects and sends Last-Event-ID header
4) the first event after resume contains the same token fragment as the last pre-glitch event

kate: Example raw SSE snippets from the client log:

# before glitch
event: message
id: 987
data: {"seq":987,"chunk":"hel"}

# after reconnect (Last-Event-ID: 987)
event: message
id: 987
data: {"seq":987,"chunk":"hel"}
event: message
id: 988
data: {"seq":988,"chunk":"lo"}

kate: Client concatenates chunks -> "helhel lo" which is wrong. This is especially visible when tokens get split across fragments.

josh: Do we know whether the server is intentionally re-emitting seq 987 or if the resume logic is supposed to skip it? Could be a server-side replay and the client should dedupe by id.

kate: Server logs show it re-sent seq 987 during resume. The server `resume` flow currently replays the last acked fragment to be safe. But clients expect either strict dedupe semantics or an id they can ignore. Browser EventSource behavior around Last-Event-ID is inconsistent across engines.

aleksandr: Two angles: server protocol and SDK behavior. Server could avoid re-emitting the last fragment when Last-Event-ID is present, or we add client-side policy to ignore the first event if its `id` == lastSeenId. For a quick fix I propose the SDK drop the first event on reconnect when ids match. Longer term we should add an atomic resume ack header so server knows where to start and won't replay.

josh: Agree. Practical path: 1) SDKs get opt-in `resumeDedup=true` which will skip first event if id matches last seen; 2) server adds `Redwood-Resume-Start` response header that indicates the next seq after resume so clients can verify; 3) add integration test that simulates a 200ms disconnect and asserts no duplication.

kate: I can add the mocha harness and raw curl logs to an issue. I noticed this also interacts badly with auth refresh: if the client refreshes token mid-reconnect we can route to a different backend that still replays cached tail fragments, making dedupe even more necessary.

aleksandr: Small SDK patch outline for node/browser: keep lastSeenId in the stream object, on reconnect set a `skipNextIfSameId` flag, then on first incoming event compare event.id to lastSeenId, if equal and flag set -> drop and clear flag. Add config toggles and metrics for dropped events.

josh: Also add test matrix across fetch/EventSource and our custom SSE parser. The parser currently emits an event per `data:` line which complicates multi-line data events. We should ensure we assemble multiline `data` correctly before exposing event.id.

kate: Filed a quick issue with details and logs. devex-bot: please create and link issue.

devex-bot: Created issue #5429: "SSE resume replay causes duplicate partial tokens; SDK should support resume dedupe" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/5429 :thumbsup:

kate: Action items: kate -> attach mocha harness and curl logs in #5429; aleksandr -> PR for SDK skipNextIfSameId flag + unit tests; josh -> coordinate server header change with infra; devex -> add e2e sim in CI.

josh: Putting this in next sprint for SDK parity work. Low-risk toggle first, protocol change after. :rocket:

aleksandr: I'll start the SDK PR now, will ping for review when ready.

kate: Thanks everyone. Hoping this will reduce the noisy duplicated fragments we've seen in a few customer traces.
